nodes.name: Robust and efficient visual odometry using colored point cloud maps via dual-sparsity and hierarchical optimization
nodes.venue: Satellite Navigation
nodes.abstract: Abstract Reliable localization is fundamental to navigation in GNSS-challenged environments, yet monocular visual odometry (VO) inevitably suffers from drift without global constraints. Point cloud maps can provide global corrections to mitigate this drift. However, existing heterogeneous feature registration methods fail to fully exploit the shared information between vision and point clouds. This limitation results in suboptimal localization accuracy, reduced robustness, and increased computational overhead. To address these issues, we propose a visual odometry system based on colored point cloud maps, which leverages both the global point cloud map as a constraint and the shared modality (color) between the colored point cloud map and the camera to ensure localization accuracy and robustness. The system consists of two main components: sparse colored point cloud construction and visual localization. In the sparse colored point cloud construction module, we introduce a map sparsification strategy that associates visual gradients with point clouds, ensuring that the retained sparse point cloud preserves salient visual gradient information, thereby reducing computational costs. This strategy is further incorporated into the vision-to-map matching stage, forming a “dual-sparsity matching” scheme. In the localization stage, we propose a hierarchical optimization-based iterative Kalman filtering algorithm, which performs multi-level iterative optimization over multi-resolution images to prevent localization from getting trapped in local optima while enhancing accuracy. Experiments on public and self-collected sequences demonstrate significant gains in both accuracy and efficiency. Compared with a representative map-based method (DSL), the proposed approach reduces ATE (RMSE) by $$52\%$$ 52 % – $$95\%$$ 95 % across multiple challenging sequences, with a representative improvement from 1.883 to $$0.152\,\text {m}$$ 0.152 m on R3live_5 ( $$91.92\%$$ 91.92 % reduction). Against the learning-based I2D-Loc++, our method achieves accuracy gains of up to $$76.6\%$$ 76.6 % and maintains robust tracking in extreme cases (e.g., R3live_3/4 ) where I2D-Loc++ and ORB-SLAM3 fail due to visual degradation. Furthermore, the system maintains near real-time efficiency, reducing total processing time by up to $$47.7\%$$ 47.7 % (e.g., from 121.11 to $$63.34\,\text {s}$$ 63.34 s on Whu_1 ). Even under severe geometric degeneracy, our tracker remains robust with an ATE of $$0.076\,\text {m}$$ 0.076 m , whereas geometry-only LiDAR–IMU localization degrades to $$9.23\,\text {m}$$ 9.23 m .

nodes.name: Enhancing sparse multi-view super-resolution with unified multi-plane image spatial representation
nodes.venue: Visual Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Abstract The popularization of multi-camera systems and multi-view image capture has led to the emergence of sparse multi-view image super-resolution (MVSR) as a promising research direction. The primary approach to sparse multi-view super-resolution (SR) currently involves extending traditional single-view SR and stereo SR frameworks, i.e., extracting features from each view and performing pixel-domain alignment and fusion to leverage cross-view reference information. However, this straightforward framework has two main drawbacks. First, performing cross-view fusion in the pixel domain disregards the spatial perception information that multi-view images provide. Second, feature alignment and fusion across views introduce considerable redundant and repetitive computations, which hinders further scalability to more viewpoints. This paper proposes a novel sparse multi-view SR framework based on a unified spatial representation reference. Specifically, the proposed method first computes a multi-plane image spatial representation from the multi-view images. This multi-plane image (MPI) representation encapsulates all the information from each view and has spatial perception. Subsequently, an upsampled reference image is rendered from the MPI representation for the low-resolution views. A high-low frequency separation fusion network is then proposed to upscale the input low-resolution images based on the rendered reference. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for recovering high-frequency details.

nodes.name: Topology-Aware Graph Learning for Cross-Field Few-Shot Stratigraphic Correlation from Well Logs
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Regional stratigraphic correlation becomes difficult when only a small number of target wells are interpreted and the well pattern is spatially uneven. This study proposes a topology-aware graph framework for cross-field few-shot stratigraphic correlation from well logs. A sequence encoder was pretrained on 87 interpreted wells from a mature source field using gamma ray, acoustic transit time, and resistivity logs. Because the source and target fields use different stratigraphic label systems, the source-specific prediction head was discarded and only the pretrained encoder was transferred; a target-specific head was then adapted using six labeled wells from a 37- well target dataset. Target wells were selected using predictive uncertainty, spatial coverage, and feature redundancy. Regional correlation was then performed on a spatial-relational graph constrained by stratigraphic order, while expert corrections were introduced as fixed anchors for controlled refinement. The framework reduced mean horizon-depth error from 2.85 m to 1.84 m, and expert-anchor refinement further reduced it to 1.51 m, an 18.0% improvement. The results show that cross-field representation transfer and topology- aware regional reasoning can reduce target-field interpretation requirements without assuming direct correspondence between source and target stratigraphic labels.

nodes.name: The Skills Intelligence Engine for an AI-Ready Energy Workforce
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract As digitalization and AI reshape the energy industry, operators must transform large technical workforces without eroding core domain expertise. The challenge goes beyond training digital specialists; it requires evolving domain professionals into domain-plus-AI, domain-plus-digital, and domain-plus-business practitioners. This paper presents a framework of energy organization's Skills Intelligence Infrastructure, a single engine linking learning activity, curated curricula, skills maps, HR data, and a conversational AI agent (beta) that bridges HR and business to support upskilling, mobility, promotion readiness, and strategic workforce planning. The infrastructure was developed through a four-layer architecture. First, a unified data foundation integrates employee learning activity with HR data, enabling segmentation by role, organization, geography, seniority, and business area. Second, curated curricula and skills maps are designed with business owners to align with enterprise priorities across AI, machine learning, data, operations, sustainability, project management, safety-critical training, sales, and domain competence. These resources support aspirational and promotion-linked roles while clarifying expectations, gaps, and priorities. Third, persona-driven experiences serve employees and managers: employees pursue pathways, identify gaps and future requirements, and build T-shaped capability—deep domain expertise broadened by AI, digital, project, and business skills—while managers monitor development, assess the regional distribution of skills, and identify talent opportunities for mobility, promotion, and hiring. Fourth, a conversational AI agent lets employees ask which skills target roles require and which pathways to prioritize, while managers evaluate talent against skills, learning records, pathway completion, and readiness indicators. Deployed across approximately 8,000 professionals, the platform delivers curated curricula for more than 60 aspirational roles, including 12 promotion-linked roles, and hundreds of pathways across digital, AI, data, project management, safety, sales, and domain expertise. As the enterprise system of record for capability, it provides end-to-end visibility into the AI upskilling funnel: more than 3,000 employees advancing their skills, more than 1,500 certified data science practitioners, and early identification of domain data scientist candidates. It surfaces more than 150 AI-powered innovation projects across the E&P lifecycle and tracks participation in an enterprise's strategic development program. For managers, it reveals skills trends across regions, business lines, and disciplines, exposing hidden capability gaps and talent opportunities. By favoring internal development over hiring, it has reduced recruitment costs for scarce digital talent and improved satisfaction with learning and career development. Unlike commercial talent-marketplace platforms, this skills-based workforce intelligence solution is purpose-built for a large technical energy workforce. It links HR and business through manager-owned skills maps, integrates siloed domain certifications and critical pathways, and operationalizes the domain-to-domain-plus-AI transformation at scale. It supports upskilling, talent conversion, mobility, promotion readiness, compliance tracking, and build-versus-hire decisions. Future enhancements will infer skills from roles, projects, and experience and extend the AI agent into talent management. This provides a foundation on which the energy workforce can build as AI reshapes the industry.

nodes.name: Scaling the Outcrop: An Integrated Cross-Scale Correlation Engine Bridging 3D Geological Outcrop Digital Twins with Subsurface Wellbore Analytics
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope In complex hydrocarbon exploration, particularly within ultra-deep or frontier plays, the scarcity of offset well data often leads to significant geological uncertainty during drilling deployment. Field outcrop studies supply the analogs used to close that gap, but an interpreted outcrop section is rarely registered to the same spatial and depth reference frame as the wells it informs. This paper reports the third development stage of a 3D geological outcrop digital twin platform — a cross-scale correlation engine that places an interpreted outcrop section onto a well's true-vertical-depth axis. It is deliberately positioned as a validation-framework contribution, not an applied field-validation study: it defines, freezes, and audits the geometry-level registration workflow and establishes the numerical control a later field campaign can test against. No paired outcrop-and-well field dataset is reported here. Methods, Procedures, Process The engine sits on an established foundation — UAV oblique photogrammetry, structure-from-motion reconstruction, RTK ground control, lithofacies segmentation — none of it claimed as new. Three elements are specified in full. A three-dimensional bedding-normal projection converts interpreted contacts to cumulative true stratigraphic thickness without assuming a section perpendicular to strike. A weighted multi-horizon affine model registers cumulative thickness to true vertical depth subsea, fitted on declared anchor horizons only. An auditable composite score ranks candidate outcrop-to-formation pairings on stratigraphic name, lithology, relative position, and marker-bed evidence. Lacking a paired field dataset, numerical behavior was examined through a disclosed synthetic benchmark: a nested ablation over 1,000 Monte Carlo realizations with ten held-out horizons, and a 4,000-trial semantic-mapping stress test with an 80-variant weight-sensitivity grid. Every parameter, equation, weight, and random seed is reported. Results, Observations, Conclusions Under the declared synthetic uncertainty model, the ablation reduced mean held-out-horizon RMSE from 4.67 m for apparent thickness tied to a single datum, to 2.01 m after three-dimensional bedding-normal projection, and to 0.27 m after four-anchor affine registration, with 98.96% empirical coverage against a nominal 95% prediction interval. The deliberately ambiguous stress test raised top-1 matching accuracy from 42.45% for name similarity alone to 91.68% for the composite score, which stayed above the name-only baseline in all 80 weight variants. These figures establish synthetic self-consistency: the equations recover a truth the generator itself constructed. They are explicitly not measurements of field accuracy, geological predictive skill, or operational efficiency. Prototype runs on a marine pilot block confirm only that the pipeline executes end to end inside a standard multi-well correlation panel. Significance/Novelty The novelty lies in integration and auditability rather than in the underlying technologies. UAV photogrammetry, SfM processing, RTK positioning, and pseudo-well construction are established practice; what is new is the reproducible chain binding them — explicit three-dimensional thickness formulation, multi-anchor depth registration, traceable semantic mapping, and a stated boundary between synthetic verification and field validation. Publishing that chain in full makes the workflow transferable rather than site-specific. A preregistered paired field campaign using these frozen equations and metrics is the declared next step.

nodes.name: Revitalizing Mature Unconventional Plays Through Machine Learning-Driven Reservoir Characterization: A Scalable Sweet Spot Detection Framework with Global Applicability
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Mature unconventional plays such as the Barnett Shale of the Fort Worth Basin still hold real, untapped potential in thin, heterogeneous intervals that fall beneath the resolution of conventional post-stack seismic inversion and were bypassed by earlier development campaigns as a result. This study presents a scalable, machine-learning (ML)-driven reservoir characterization framework built to resolve these thin-bed sweet spots and to generalize to analogous plays worldwide, including emerging unconventional targets across the Middle East and North Africa. Petrophysical logs from the V2P and E4P wells were quality-controlled with unsupervised anomaly-detection algorithms, then used to derive Total Organic Carbon (TOC, via Schmoker's density relationship) and a Brittleness Index (from normalized Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio). Spectral decomposition of the 3D seismic volume enhanced vertical resolution below conventional seismic bandwidth, and the resulting frequency-dependent attributes were combined with conventional seismic attributes into a multi-attribute feature space. We benchmarked eight supervised regression algorithms and nine classification algorithms across six performance metrics (R2, MSE, MAE, RMSLE, MAPE, and training time) to select the optimal predictive engine. The Extra Tree Regressor gave the strongest performance for elastic-property prediction, and the Extra Tree Classifier exceeded 90 percent accuracy in binary sweet-spot classification, ahead of every other algorithm benchmarked. A multi-criteria qualification standard (P-impedance below 12,000; S-impedance below 6,000; Poisson's ratio between 0.15 and 0.35; Brittleness Index at or above 35 percent; TOC above 2 weight percent), applied volumetrically, identified previously unrecognized reservoir intervals within the Upper Barnett member: an approximately 2-meter interval at V2P below the 19-millisecond window, and an approximately 2.5-meter interval at E4P below the 35-millisecond window both undetectable by conventional deterministic inversion. Geocellular modeling confirmed the lateral continuity of these compartments across the study area. This work is among the first to couple spectral-decomposition-enhanced seismic attributes with ML-driven elastic-property modeling to resolve shale sweet spots as thin as 2.0 to 2.5 meters. Because the classification framework is physics-grounded and needs only limited additional data once calibrated at well control, it is directly transferable to other mature unconventional basins, giving operators a practical route to recovering bypassed reserves and extending field life without the cost of new 3D seismic acquisition.

nodes.name: Machine Learning-Based Virtual Flow Meter for Oil Rate Estimation and Production Back-Allocation in a Mature Giant Onshore Carbonate Field
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate well-level oil-rate estimates underpin production surveillance, reservoir management, production optimization, and back-allocation. In mature fields with large well stocks, continuous well-level metering is frequently unavailable because of cost, infrastructure, maintenance, and operational constraints, and well rates are instead obtained from periodic production tests. This leaves a visibility gap between tests during which choke changes, pressure fluctuations, and water-cut or gas-oil-ratio evolution are not reflected in reported rates. This paper presents a practical, explainable machine-learning workflow that estimates well-level oil rate for naturally flowing wells using only routinely available production-test and operating data. The study is based on 2,816 approved production-test records acquired over a 24-month period from 280 naturally flowing wells in a mature giant onshore carbonate field (Field A). Model inputs were choke size, wellhead pressure (WHP), flowline pressure (FLP), water cut (WC), gas-oil ratio (GOR), and an engineered pressure-differential feature (ΔP = WHP − FLP). To reflect realistic deployment conditions, WC and GOR were taken from the most recent preceding tests rather than from the test being predicted. Twelve regression algorithms were benchmarked using R2, mean absolute error (MAE), root-mean-squared error (RMSE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Under a record-level 60/20/20 split, nonlinear ensemble tree models clearly outperformed linear and regularized regressors. Although ExtraTrees achieved marginally higher accuracy, it produced a perfect training fit; Random Forest was therefore selected as the deployment model for its comparable accuracy, smaller generalization gap, and interpretability. The selected model achieved a validation R2 of 0.818 and a hold-out test R2 of 0.811, with hold-out MAE of 240 STB/D and RMSE of 363 STB/D. Model behavior was examined using three independent explainability methods—impurity-based importance, permutation importance, and SHAP—which consistently identified choke size, water cut, and pressure differential as the dominant predictors, in agreement with choke-flow and nodal-analysis principles. Five field cases based on new tests not used in model development showed that the ML estimates were markedly closer to subsequent multiphase-flow-meter (MPFM) measurements than the interim allocation estimates, with case errors between 0.3% and 8.5%. The workflow operates entirely on existing field data without additional sensors, physics simulators, or synthetic training data, and is currently being extended to additional fields. It is intended as a surveillance and allocation-support tool that complements—rather than replaces—validated well testing and fiscal metering. Priority enhancements include well-blind and time-forward validation, prediction-uncertainty estimation, and artificial-lift-specific and physics-guided models.

nodes.name: Machine Learning-Based Reservoir Facies Classification and Exploration Implications of Mesozoic Volcanic Buried Hills in the Bohai Bay Basin, Northern China
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Mesozoic volcanic buried hill oilfields have gradually become important targets for medium-deep oil and gas replacement in the Bohai Bay Basin, northern China. Drilling Stem Testing (DST) results of two adjacent wells in Block Q show several-fold differences in productivity, which are attributed to strong heterogeneity of volcanic rocks ranging from volcanic lavas to pyroclastic rocks and from basic to acidic compositions. The controlling factors of reservoir quality are not static; instead, the dominant controlling factors shift with variations in lithology, lithofacies, fractures, and petrophysical properties. Based on core data, conventional well logging, and imaging logging, 18 lithologies were identified, and classified into eruptive facies and overflow facies. Eruptive facies include andesitic volcanic breccia, volcanic breccia, rhyolitic volcanic breccia, crystalline tuff, and andesitic tuff. The overflow facies comprise (altered) basalt, rhyolite, dacite, (altered) andesite, and trachyandesite. Lithology identification templates were established by integrating thin-section observations, core data, conventional logging, and imaging logging, providing a critical reference for efficient lithology identification in the study area in the future. Meanwhile, fractures were identified and quantified using imaging logging. Effective fractures include vuggy open, fully open, and partially open fractures, while ineffective fractures include clay-filled fractures and (calcite or quartz) cemented fractures. In the vertical zonation (weathered zone, transition zone, and inner zone), reservoirs with variable fracture orientations exhibit better connectivity than those with consistent fracture orientations. Two machine-learning facies classification methods were evaluated, and the indexed and probabilized self-organizing map (IPSOM) demonstrated superior performance for reservoir facies classification. Eight sensitive variables were selected: NMR permeability, effective porosity, secondary porosity, compressional slowness, fracture aperture, fracture length, fracture porosity, and fracture density. Eight reservoir facies were labeled IP1 to IP8: IP1 tight, IP2 high porosity-strong vuggy facies, IP3 medium porosity-fractured facies, IP4 medium porosity-fractured facies, IP5 fractured-tight facies, IP6 high porosity-fractured facies, IP7 fractured-strong vuggy facies, and IP8 vuggy-high porosity facies. The reservoir quality ranks: IP6 > IP8 > IP2 > IP7 > IP4 > IP3 > IP5 > IP1. Then, these results were used for supervised machine learning to classify reservoir facies in two additional wells (Q1-4 and Q2-1) lacking NMR data or fracture evaluation data. IPSOM facies show a strong correlation with reservoir quality and storage-flow capacity, while testing results indicate that hydrocarbon productivity is additionally controlled by charge, migration pathways, and trap effectiveness. The proportions of favorable reservoir facies (IP6, IP8, and IP2) in Wells Q1-4, Q3-1, and Q2-1 are 72%, 34.8%, and 16.2%, respectively, and Well Q1-4 recovered both oil and water during formation testing, Well Q1-3 produces mainly water with no oil or gas, while Well Q2-1 is essentially a dry well. This study provides an innovative integrated method for lithology, fracture, and intelligent reservoir facies classification in heterogeneous volcanic buried hills, supporting reliable productivity prediction and supporting reservoir quality prediction and exploration risk evaluation in Mesozoic volcanic buried-hill reservoirs.

nodes.name: Machine Learning Approach for Synthetic Sonic and Density Log Generation in Kuwait Field with Lithological Data Integration
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract This paper presents and validates robust machine learning workflows for generating synthetic sonic (DTCO, DTSM) and density logs (BD) in support of drilling optimization and wellbore stability analysis, demonstrating improved prediction accuracy through formation-specific model training and flexible data integration across subsurface formations of Field X in Kuwait. The proposed pipeline leverages well log data from offset wells to develop localized predictive models for target wells within the same geologic context. Input features include gamma ray logs, surface drilling parameters, and lithological volume fractions. Spatial orientation techniques are introduced during feature engineering to capture vertical continuity and spatial relationships that conventional approaches often overlook. Rather than relying on a single generalized model, the framework trains dedicated formation-specific models applied in sequence, optimized through hyperparameter tuning, and validated through a leave-one-out cross-validation methodology using Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), correlation scores, and visual assessments. The framework delivers significant improvements in synthetic log generation across all evaluated formations in Field X. Spatial orientation techniques prove instrumental in enhancing prediction quality over conventional point-wise methods by effectively capturing formation continuity that generalized approaches miss. The sequential formation-specific modeling strategy consistently outperforms single generalized models, with each dedicated model adapting to the distinct geological characteristics of its target formation, yielding high correlation values and low error metrics across diverse settings. The integration of lithological volume fractions delivers meaningful accuracy gains throughout the field, most notably in formations where earlier models underperformed, such as Formation 6, while further improving results in formations like Formation 1-3. Reliability is confirmed through post-hoc comparison against real measurements across all formations, demonstrating that the framework produces valid synthetic logs suitable for practical use in drilling and wellbore stability workflows. This work introduces a formation-specific sequential modeling framework as a safe and cost-efficient alternative to conventional sonic and density log acquisition, using offset well data to generate field-specific synthetic logs. By demonstrating the added value of integrating lithological volume fractions alongside drilling parameters, this approach advances machine learning-assisted geomechanical characterization of subsurface formations.

nodes.name: Lightweight Edge AI Agent for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Distributed Acoustic Sensing
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) systems generate large volumes of spatiotemporal data that challenge conventional cloud-centric monitoring architectures. Transmitting continuous DAS telemetry for centralized analysis introduces bandwidth, latency, and operational constraints, particularly in remote energy infrastructure environments. This paper presents a lightweight unsupervised edge AI agent for real-time anomaly detection operating on DAS measurements and derived multi-domain feature streams. The proposed framework integrates anomaly scoring, spatiotemporal clustering, trajectory-coherence validation, event severity assessment, autonomous action generation, online memory adaptation, and safety-aware state management within a unified edge-deployable architecture. An agentic processing loop performs perception, anomaly evaluation, event validation, action selection, learning, and safety monitoring while maintaining bounded computational requirements suitable for continuous field deployment. Coherent anomaly events are identified using spatial and temporal consistency criteria, enabling suppression of isolated artifacts and transient noise while preserving operationally meaningful patterns. Detected events are transformed into compact event-centric payloads containing severity, temporal extent, spatial extent, and decision metadata, substantially reducing communication requirements relative to raw data transmission. The framework further incorporates operational trust mechanisms including signed agent manifests, execution-path control, runtime watchdog monitoring, and fail-safe operating modes to support secure and reliable deployment in industrial environments. The framework was evaluated using synthetic datasets and real DAS datasets from field applications, including injection monitoring and microseismic event detection. Results demonstrate effective detection and prioritization of coherent spatiotemporal events without requiring labeled training data. Event-centric reporting reduced communication requirements by 94.36% while processing 1500 DAS channels with a peak memory footprint of 4.83 MB and an average latency below 1 s. The measured performance supports real-time edge deployment without dedicated accelerator hardware. The proposed framework enables scalable, explainable, and communication-efficient DAS monitoring by bringing intelligent event detection, validation, and decision support directly to the network edge.

nodes.name: From Routine Fixed Schedules to Signals: A Condition-Responsive, AI-Augmented Pigging Intelligence Framework for Localised Internal Corrosion Control in Crude Oil and Water Injection Pipelines
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Pigging plans in most operating companies globally are scheduled by calendar days. Pipeline segments are pigged every 30, 60 or 90 days based on the historical fixed maintenance schedules set during commissioning, regardless of the real time corrosion dynamics of the pipeline when in service. However, in most crude oil and water injection lines where the corrosion environment shifts with well stream composition, throughput and bacteria activity, the fixed schedule methodology of pigging does not prevent escalation of corrosion events. A five-year trending of several pipeline ILI data shows why 63% of anomalies deeper than 18% wall thickness were found in segments fully compliant with their pigging schedule. A 24-month study across 312 km length of pipelines compared condition-responsive segments against fixed 30-day controls showed that the mean maximum pit depth growth fell by 54.5% with over 80% drop in reactive integrity actions. Furthermore, the chemical inhibitor wetting efficiency increased by 18 points with 22.5% reduction in pigging runs. More so, 78% of the anomaly's clusters were located at the 5 to 7 o'clock orientation and concentrated in pipelines where inhibitor wetting had dropped below 69%. Sulphate Reducing Bacteria (SRB) and Iron Oxidizing Bacteria (IOB) counts proved the strongest leading indicators in the corrosion index, which is what should be expected in MIC-susceptible water injection systems. This paper proposes and validates the Pigging Intelligence Framework (PIF), in which pig runs are triggered by corrosion signals rather than fixed maintenance schedules. The PIF has three layers namely: the Corrosion Signal Index (CSI), supervised machine learning model and a root cause framework. The CSI combines flow velocity, BS&W content, microbiological activity, inhibitor residuals and ILI pit depth progression into a continuously updated risk score for each segment. Furthermore, the supervised machine learning model, trained on five years of pigging records and post-pig debris analytics from the pipelines, identifies the leading indicators of accelerated pitting. A root cause investigation tool anchored in NACE SP0106 ensures every unacceptable corrosion event produces a traceable corrective action, with outputs mapped to SAP PM and the integrity database. The study posits that pigging should be timed, based on the state of the pipeline and integrity condition of the medium rather than pigging as a historical norm. Therefore, it put forwards an A.I augmented framework in which pigging frequency, chemical dosing and inspection strategy recalibrate continuously from model output, closing the loop between detection, diagnosis and action.

nodes.name: First Time Deployment in UAE: Successful Mapping the Water-Flood Front Using the New UDAR 3D Lookahead Reservoir Mapping in Horizontal Oil Producer Well, Case Study Onshore UAE
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Early identification and mitigation of water-front risk is critical when drilling development and infill wells in mature carbonate fields. Uncertainty related to fluid distribution, dynamic water movement, and proximity to swept zones can lead to sub-optimal well placement, early water breakthrough, and reduced well productivity. Conventional Ultra Deep Azimuthal Resistivity (UDAR) is limited to map the risks around the wellbore only. This paper presents the first-time deployment of new UDAR 3D lookahead reservoir mapping technology in UAE for real-time identification of water-front risk while drilling a horizontal oil producer well. The subject well targets thick carbonate reservoirs layer with known water encroachment risk. by drilling a single 8 ½" inch, horizontal section. The planned footage was approximately 3500 feet measured depth. Consequently, a 6 ¾" inch UDAR 3D lookahead tool has been combined with a triple combo bottom hole assembly included Gamma Ray, Density and Neutron porosity for comprehensive formation evaluation and enhancing the well placement, with the aim of simultaneous geosteering and Fluid reservoir mapping using advanced ahead of the bit 3D inversion processing in real-time. The new UDAR 3D lookahead allows more precise decisions by early detecting the risk of water ahead of bit and avoiding sidetrack of water influx. Also, facilitating smoother wellbore. The new UDAR ahead of bit reservoir mapping, transmitter was closer to the bit and placed within the rotary Steerable System (RSS) at 9 feet from bit allowing UDAR 3D near bit and up to 30 feet ahead of bit for early detecting the water-front and provide proactive decision. In addition, actual Shallow Phase / Attenuation Resistivity measurements, which helped in providing faster estimation of Water Saturation closer to bit. For the first time in the UAE and in carbonate reservoir, The new UDAR 3D ahead of bit reservoir mapping has successfully mapped water flood ahead of bit up to 12 ft. with water saturation of 45%. It has provided Continuous real-time 3D lookahead reservoir mapping with 100% streaming aided in improving reservoir insight and enhance proactive Geosteering decisions. It helped with a proactive decision and drilled 2959 feet out of 3500 feet due to high water saturation ahead of bit. In addition, provided Near-bit multi frequency compensated resistivity for formation evaluation and Saturation estimation. The new UDAR 3D ahead of bit reservoir mapping. The real-time inversion data supported identification of zones associated with increased water-front risk, allowing timely interpretation during drilling operations. Key observations include: Detection of deep resistivity contrasts consistent with fluid variationsImproved confidence in identifying potential water-encroached zones ahead of the bitEnhanced situational awareness compared with conventional near-wellbore measurementsSupport for informed real-time geosteering decisions to mitigate water risk This case study demonstrates the successful first application of the new UDAR 3D ahead of bit reservoir mapping in carbonate reservoir. Onshore. The results demonstrated the value of optimizing lateral lengths and sustaining the production on well scale, and scale it up and optimize the field development plan.

nodes.name: Enhancing 3D Static Geological Models Using Unsupervised Machine Learning (IPSOM) for Rock Typing: A North Oman Case Study
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Reliable rock typing is fundamental to static reservoir modelling, but conventional methods often struggle in thin-bedded, heterogeneous clastic reservoirs where subtle lithological changes cannot be fully captured from core data alone. In the Shammar reservoir of North Oman, this limitation added significant uncertainty to facies distribution, petrophysical modelling, and hydrocarbon volume estimates, with a direct impact on field development planning. Conventional deterministic workflows often grouped intervals with different flow characteristics into the same rock class because the available data could not distinguish subtle differences in reservoir quality. As development progressed, this reduced confidence in the static model and pointed to the need for a more objective way to represent reservoir heterogeneity while staying consistent with geological observations and production behaviour. This study presents a workflow that applies an Iterative Probabilistic Self-Organizing Map (IPSOM), an unsupervised machine learning technique, to classify electrofacies from standardized well-log data. The workflow combines quality-controlled wireline logs, core measurements, and production data to generate data-driven rock types, which were then checked against core observations, Production Logging Tool (PLT) data, and dynamic field performance. Before clustering, the datasets were quality-controlled, environmentally corrected, depth-matched, and normalized to ensure consistency across the field. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was used to assess how much each logging parameter contributed to the clustering and to identify which variables gave the best discrimination between electrofacies. The resulting electrofacies were built into a three-dimensional static geological model to improve facies distribution, petrophysical modelling, reservoir characterization, and uncertainty assessment, while keeping the model consistent with dynamic production behaviour. The workflow identified three electrofacies: Excellent Rock, Good Rock, and Non-Reservoir. Compared with the previous modelling approach, the IPSOM-derived facies gave a better representation of vertical heterogeneity and reservoir continuity and reduced interpreter bias. Facies-dependent saturation-height functions increased the Base Case STOIIP estimate by 4.3%, improved the match with historical production, and made it easier to identify reservoir flow units and bypassed pay. The updated model also supported ranking of future infill drilling opportunities with greater confidence. Independent checks showed good agreement between the electrofacies classification, core descriptions, PLT observations, and production history, confirming that the electrofacies reflected real geological differences rather than statistical clustering alone. Wells intersecting a larger proportion of the Excellent Rock facies consistently showed higher injectivity and better production performance, adding further confidence in the workflow. The study shows that IPSOM offers a practical, repeatable, and scalable way to classify electrofacies in heterogeneous clastic reservoirs. Combining machine learning with conventional geological interpretation, petrophysics, and production data improves the reliability of static models, reduces uncertainty in reservoir characterization, and supports better-informed development decisions. The method is not intended to replace geological workflows but to give them a more objective, data-driven basis for combining multiple subsurface datasets. It is readily transferable to other mature clastic reservoirs where conventional rock typing cannot capture fine-scale heterogeneity.

nodes.name: Edge AI Vision Camera Intelligence and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) for Real-Time Industrial Safety Monitoring in Oil & Gas Facilities
nodes.venue: ADIPEC
nodes.abstract: Abstract Objectives/Scope Oil & gas operations require continuous monitoring of safety compliance and high risk anomalies; however, conventional supervision and manual CCTV monitoring are constrained by limited coverage, delayed detection, and inconsistent enforcement. This paper presents an AI-based industrial safety monitoring framework for edge computer vision analytics and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) to enable real-time detection of safety violations and hazardous conditions. Methods, Procedures, Process The proposed solution integrates deep learning-based video analytics with existing CCTV infrastructure and AMR-mounted cameras to extend monitoring into blind spots and dynamic work zones. AI inference is performed on edge GPU servers to ensure low latency, reduce cloud dependency, and support uninterrupted site operations. The platform detects over 100 industrial safety anomaly types, including PPE non-compliance, restricted zone intrusion, work-at-height violations, fire/smoke indicators, spill/leak anomalies, housekeeping deviations. Temporal tracking and Multi-frame validation is applied to improve event confidence and reduce transient false triggers. Rule-based escalation workflows generate real-time alerts with timestamped evidence frames, which are stored in an auditable event database for compliance reporting, trend analytics, and continuous improvement. Results, Observations, Conclusions Performance evaluation across operational deployments indicates a detection accuracy of 90-95% depending on use case complexity and environmental conditions. End-to-end alert latency from detection to notification was measured at approximately 3 seconds, enabling near real-time intervention by EHS teams. The combined CCTV + AMR monitoring approach improved coverage in areas where fixed cameras had occlusion limitations, particularly in large fabrication yards, laydown zones, and high-traffic operational corridors. Observed deployment constraints included low-light sensitivity, PPE partial visibility and false triggers caused by reflections and steam. These were mitigated through site-specific confidence threshold tuning, improved zoning logic, and periodic model refinement using operational datasets. The system also enabled automated reporting outputs such as violation heatmaps, repeat violation identification, shift-wise compliance scoring, and incident categorization. The paper concludes that integrating edge AI vision with existing CCTV infrastructure and AMR-based mobile sensing provides a scalable and measurable approach to proactive industrial safety monitoring, improving response time, compliance governance, and data-driven EHS decision-making. Novel/Additive Information This paper presents additive field evidence on deploying a low-latency (~3 seconds) edge AI vision system integrated with existing CCTV networks and Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) to monitor 100+ industrial safety anomalies. It contributes practical deployment methodology, performance benchmarking (90-95% accuracy), and mitigation strategies for real operating constraints such as occlusion, low-light, reflections, and steam. The work advances scalable, audit-ready AI safety intelligence for petroleum operations.

nodes.name: Classification of Flood-Prone Areas in Padang City Using Landsat-9 Satellite Imagery
nodes.venue: Journal of Multidisciplinary Science: MIKAILALSYS
nodes.abstract: Flood-susceptibility mapping requires spatial information that captures the combined influence of hydrological conditions, topography, soils, and land cover. This study classified and mapped flood-prone areas in Padang City by integrating six parameters: rainfall, elevation, slope, distance from rivers, soil type, and land use/land cover. A quantitative spatial approach using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) was employed. Land cover was classified from Landsat-9 Collection 2 Level-2 imagery using the Classification and Regression Trees (CART) algorithm in Google Earth Engine. The six parameters were subsequently scored, weighted, and integrated through weighted-overlay analysis. The land-cover classification achieved an overall accuracy of 85.17%, while the overlay analysis delineated five flood-susceptibility classes. Moderate susceptibility occupied the largest area, covering 30,675.414 ha (45.79%), followed by high susceptibility at 17,631.140 ha (26.32%), low susceptibility at 17,226.524 ha (25.72%), very high susceptibility at 1,420.275 ha (2.12%), and very low susceptibility at 31.048 ha (0.05%). These findings reveal substantial spatial variation in flood susceptibility across Padang City, with moderate susceptibility predominating. The study provides an integrated spatial assessment to support disaster mitigation and environmentally responsive land-use planning.

nodes.name: Depth-adaptive suppression of subject-dependent interference for robust cross-subject EEG emotion recognition
nodes.venue: Biomedical Engineering / Biomedizinische Technik
nodes.abstract: Abstract Objectives Cross-subject electroencephalography (EEG) emotion recognition is limited by inter-subject variability, which embeds subject-specific nuisance information in learned representations and reduces generalization to unseen individuals. Methods We propose a two-stage layer-adaptive subject-interference suppression framework built on EEG Conformer. In the search stage, differentiable gates and adversarial subject classifiers are attached to hierarchical representations from the patch embedding layer and Transformer blocks to estimate where subject information is most strongly encoded. The top-ranked layers are then fixed and the model is retrained for final emotion classification. A subject-aware supervised contrastive regularizer is further used to improve label-consistent cross-subject representation learning. Results Experiments on SEED under strict leave-one-subject-out evaluation show improved performance over representative machine-learning, domain-adaptation, and deep-learning baselines. Auxiliary experiments on SEED-IV indicate adaptability under a more challenging label setting. Layer-wise probing shows that subject-specific information remains decodable across depths but is relatively stronger in shallow and early intermediate representations. Conclusions Selective depth-aware suppression provides a practical and interpretable strategy for robust EEG-based affective brain–computer interfaces.

nodes.name: OGRR-Net: observation-guided residual refinement learning for photoacoustic imaging
nodes.venue: Optics Express
nodes.abstract: Photoacoustic imaging provides optical-absorption contrast through ultrasonic detection. However, image reconstruction remains affected by acquisition geometry, detector response, acoustic noise, and the attenuation of high-frequency components during analytic inversion. Although deep post-processing methods have shown effectiveness in artifact reduction, purely image-domain restoration lacks a direct mechanism for incorporating complementary information contained in the raw measurement data. This work proposes OGRR-Net, an observation-guided residual refinement network for photoacoustic imaging. The network takes an initial reconstruction as the spatial reference and encodes the corresponding raw sinogram into an observation-guidance map, which conditions a gated residual correction pathway for image refinement. Evaluated on an in vivo mouse dataset and the OADAT optoacoustic dataset against representative image-domain and hybrid reconstruction methods, the proposed observation-guided strategy improves reconstruction fidelity, reduces artifacts, and enhances the preservation of structural details.

nodes.name: Physics-guided machine learning for predicting complete tool influence functions in flexible ball-end polishing
nodes.venue: Optics Express
nodes.abstract: The tool influence function (TIF) is fundamental to computer-controlled optical surfacing (CCOS) for deterministic material removal. Conventional TIF acquisition relies on either physics-based modeling with extensive parameter calibration or time-consuming spot experiments. Existing machine learning studies in polishing have mainly focused on scalar removal-rate prediction, while direct prediction of the complete radial TIF profile from pre-settable process parameters remains insufficiently explored. In this work, we propose a physics-guided machine-learning framework for end-to-end prediction of complete TIF radial profiles in flexible ball-end polishing from four controllable process parameters: normal load, spindle speed, pad hardness, and abrasive concentration. Physics-guided feature engineering, derived from the Preston equation and Hertz contact theory, expands the 4-dimensional raw parameter space into an 11-dimensional physics-informed feature space. A dual-model framework is then developed by combining two complementary physics-constrained gradient boosting regression (PC-GBR) models through equal-weight averaging. In PC-GBR, physical prior knowledge derived from the Preston equation and Hertz contact theory is incorporated through monotonic constraints on selected physics-guided features. Based on 53 valid replicate measurements aggregated into 15 operating-condition groups, the proposed framework is validated by leave-one-group-out cross-validation. It achieves a Peak MAPE of 7.5%, an MRR MAPE of 7.9%, and a mean Profile R2 of 0.948. Physics-guided feature engineering reduces MRR prediction error by 45% relative to raw inputs, and the predicted radial profile can be directly reconstructed into a full two-dimensional TIF for CCOS dwell-time computation.

nodes.name: Neglected Open-Globe Injury and Limb Amputation Following a Blast Explosion in a Pediatric Polytrauma Patient: An Observational Analytic Case Study on Delayed Ophthalmic Intervention, Ocular Trauma Score Dynamics, and Health System Barriers in Remote Eastern Indonesia
nodes.venue: Bioscientia Medicina : Journal of Biomedicine and Translational Research
nodes.abstract: Background: Blast-related ocular trauma in children in archipelagic developing regions is a devastating, multimechanistic emergency, often complicated by systemic polytrauma prioritization and geographical referral barriers. Objective: To characterize the clinical trajectory, Ocular Trauma Score dynamics, and health-system barriers of a neglected pediatric open-globe blast injury with concomitant traumatic hand amputation in remote eastern Indonesia. Methods: A 13-year-old boy presented 5 days after a homemade fish-bomb explosion. Evaluation used Birmingham Eye Trauma Terminology (BETT) classification, longitudinal biomicroscopy, acoustic B-scan ultrasonography, quantitative Ocular Trauma Score (OTS) and modified Pediatric OTS, and multi-level structural barrier assessment. Results: At presentation (Day 5), right eye (OD) visual acuity was light perception with intraocular pressure of 7 mmHg, full-thickness superior eyelid margin laceration, total dark hyphema (Grade IV), and traumatic corneal scars, while the left eye (OS) maintained 20/20 vision with multiple corneal foreign bodies. Acoustic B-scan OD revealed complete funnel-shaped retinal detachment tethered to the optic disc and dense vitreous hemorrhage. OD calculated an OTS raw score of 12 (Category 1, 74% no-light-perception probability). Following surgical delays driven by maritime transit and BPJS insurance administrative bottlenecks, 1-week follow-up (Day 12) revealed fulminant corneal keratolysis with diffuse stromal melting, chemosis, and cicatricial eyelid notch, whereas OS achieved complete corneal re-epithelialization. Conclusion: Neglected pediatric blast ocular trauma leads to accelerated enzymatic keratolysis and irreversible functional amaurosis when systemic polytrauma prioritizes limb salvage over sight. Integrating mandatory ophthalmic triage into rural disaster protocols is critical.

Feasibility Analysis of Education in Indonesian Provinces: A Machine Learning Clustering Approach for Regional Classification
nodes.venue: Engineering and Technology Journal
nodes.abstract: Education system feasibility varies significantly across Indonesian provinces due to geographic, socioeconomic, and infrastructural disparities. This study applies unsupervised machine learning clustering algorithms (K-Means, Hierarchical Clustering, Gaussian Mixture Models, and Self-Organizing Maps) to classify Indonesian provinces into homogeneous groups based on education feasibility indicators. Using 39 provinces and special territories, we evaluated clustering quality through internal validation metrics (Silhouette coefficient and Davies-Bouldin index) and inter-algorithm agreement measures (Adjusted Rand Index and Normalized Mutual Information). Results demonstrate that Hierarchical Clustering achieves the best Davies-Bouldin index (0.782), while K-Means and GMM produce identical partitions (ARI = 1.0, NMI = 1.0). Self-Organizing Maps identified nine distinct regional education feasibility profiles, with provincial distributions revealing significant heterogeneity in education conditions. These findings provide a quantitative framework for targeted policy interventions and resource allocation to improve education feasibility across Indonesia’s diverse regions.

nodes.name: Dual‐Mode Optical Temperature Sensing of Mg <sub>0.75</sub> Al <sub>2.16</sub> O <sub>4</sub> : Cr <sup>3</sup> <sup>+</sup> /Er <sup>3</sup> <sup>+</sup> Transparent Ceramic With Spatial Separation Structure
nodes.venue: Journal of the American Ceramic Society
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Designing the energy transfer process between activator ions is an effective strategy for achieving multimodal, high‐sensitivity fluorescent temperature sensing. Herein, a dual‐mode fluorescent temperature sensor was developed based on the Mg 0.75 Al 2.16 O 4 : 0.1at%Cr 3+ /0.03at%Er 3+ transparent ceramic. Spatial separation of Cr 3+ /Er 3+ ions was achieved by utilizing both the lattice and grain boundary environments within the transparent ceramic. Within this unique structure, efficient energy transfer from Er 3+ to Cr 3+ was established. As a result, Cr 3+ emitted near‐infrared upconversion fluorescence peaking at 797 nm ( 4 T 2 level) under 980 nm laser excitation. The downconversion fluorescence lifetime of Cr 3+ and the upconversion fluorescence intensity ratio of Cr 3+ /Er 3+ can serve as temperature sensing signals. Within the range of 300–573 K, the maximum relative sensitivity reached 4.2% K −1 . This work demonstrates the potential for designing functional ionic spatial structures within transparent ceramics.

nodes.name: Model‐based image restoration targeting higher‐dose digital mammography: Impact on radiologists' detection of clustered microcalcifications
nodes.venue: Medical Physics
nodes.abstract: Abstract Background Image noise in digital mammography (DM) can obscure image details and reduce the detectability of clinically relevant findings such as microcalcifications. Purpose To present and evaluate an extended model‐based (MB) image restoration pipeline for DM that incorporates quantum, electronic, and structural noise components, as well as spatial noise correlation, and to assess its effect on breast radiologists' detection of simulated microcalcification clusters in clinical mammograms. Methods A total of 120 clinical DM images acquired using a GE Senographe Pristina system were used. Simulated microcalcification clusters were inserted into locally dense fibroglandular regions at controlled contrast levels. The restoration pipeline was configured to target the signal and noise characteristics predicted by the model for an acquisition at approximately twice the original radiation dose. Six breast radiologists with different levels of experience, classified as Junior or Senior, participated in two human observer experiments: (i) a pilot study using original clinical images with simulated clusters and a four‐alternative forced‐choice (4AFC) protocol combined with a three‐down‐one‐up (3D1U) staircase to estimate reader‐specific contrast detection thresholds and achieve comparable baseline task difficulty across readers; and (ii) a main 4AFC observer study using individualized datasets generated according to each reader's estimated contrast threshold, in which microcalcification detection performance was compared between the original and restored image conditions based on the percentage of correct responses (PC). Two generalized linear mixed models (GLMMs) were used: the first evaluated the effect of image condition as a fixed effect, with reader and case as crossed random intercepts, and the second evaluated the effect of reader experience on detection performance in the original image condition. Results At the reader‐specific contrast thresholds estimated in the pilot study, the mean PC for the original images was 78.3%, within the prespecified target performance range. Mean PC increased to 84.3% for the restored images, corresponding to an absolute improvement of 6.0 percentage points. The primary GLMM indicated a significant restoration effect on detection performance (OR = 1.57, 95% CI: 1.15–2.14, ). Baseline mean PC was 78.7% for Junior readers and 78.0% for Senior readers, and the separate GLMM found no evidence of an experience‐group effect under the original image condition (). Conclusions The proposed extended MB restoration pipeline improved the detectability of simulated microcalcification clusters by breast radiologists under the controlled 4AFC conditions investigated. By targeting the signal and noise characteristics predicted by the model for an acquisition at approximately twice the original radiation dose without requiring additional radiation exposure, the method represents a promising approach for improving microcalcification detectability in DM.

nodes.name: Eyegent: Visual Attention Orchestration on Concepts
nodes.venue: International Journal of Computer Vision
nodes.abstract: Abstract Where a human looks is not random, nor is it merely a reflex to visual salience. It is a decision shaped by goals, constrained by language, and driven by the need to resolve uncertainty. We propose Eyegent , an active vision agent built on this premise: that visual search is best understood as sequential Bayesian inference over semantically grounded hypotheses, with fixations serving as epistemic actions. Given an image and a natural-language query, Eyegent constructs a discrete hypothesis space of candidate segmentation masks, maintains an explicit posterior belief distribution, and selects each fixation to maximise expected information gain—updating beliefs via vision–language model verification and terminating when uncertainty falls below a principled risk threshold. We formalise this process as Bayesian Active Semantic Grounding (BASG), a computational-level account that provides formal guarantees on belief concentration, entropy reduction, and bounded decision risk. The framework is neurobiologically grounded in the large-scale network organisation of the human brain, with the Salience Network identified as the dynamic orchestrator of semantic, inferential, and oculomotor processes. Critically, Eyegent requires no gaze supervision and no task-specific training: it is zero-shot, modular, and built entirely from off-the-shelf components. Evaluated on RefCOCO-Gaze and AiR-D, two benchmarks coupling language-driven visual tasks with human eye-tracking ground truth, Eyegent achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance among zero-shot methods across semantic, spatial, and structural scanpath metrics, and approaches supervised baselines on several dimensions. The result is a system that does not merely predict where humans look, but generates scanpaths for the same reason humans generate them: to find out.

nodes.name: Antenatal diagnosis and classification for placenta accreta (adherence) spectrum: Clinical practice guideline and recommendations by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine and the Perinatal Medicine Foundation
nodes.venue: Pregnancy
nodes.abstract: Abstract This practical guidance was developed by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine in collaboration with the Perinatal Medicine Foundation to support antenatal diagnosis and clinical management in pregnancies at risk for placenta accreta spectrum (PAS). It provides an evidence‐informed approach to screening, diagnosis, referral, and peripartum planning across healthcare settings with different resources. PAS is increasingly encountered alongside rising cesarean delivery rates, use of in vitro fertilization, and a history of uterine surgery. It remains associated with severe maternal morbidity, including massive hemorrhage, large‐volume transfusion, uterine rupture, peripartum hysterectomy, pelvic organ injury, intensive care admission, and maternal death. Early recognition and multidisciplinary care are therefore central to management. Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) is considered a potential precursor of PAS. Women with a low implantation site and a previous cesarean delivery are at increased risk. Early transvaginal ultrasound is advised in women with a previous cesarean delivery to establish the implantation site, identify CSP, and support counseling and timely consideration of uterine‐preserving treatment. In the second and third trimesters, combined transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasound assesses placental location, myometrial thickness and contour, and the uterovesical interface. Sonographic markers include placental lacunae, placental bulge, uterovesical hypervascularity, and bridging vessels, which may occur individually or in combination. Two‐dimensional grayscale ultrasound is the mainstay of antenatal assessment, supported by color Doppler; three‐dimensional imaging may provide additional information in selected specialist settings. Magnetic resonance imaging has a complementary role when ultrasound is inconclusive, placental location is non‐anterior or non‐previa, or technical factors limit visualization. Suspected CSP or PAS should prompt referral to a perinatal center with multidisciplinary expertise, blood product support, adult and neonatal intensive care, and access to complex pelvic surgery. Delivery timing and surgical preparation should be individualized.

nodes.name: EBM-Nav: energy-based model for zero-shot visual navigation via implicit scene representation
nodes.venue: Journal of King Saud University Computer and Information Sciences
nodes.abstract: Abstract Zero-shot visual navigation enables agents to generalize to unseen environments without task-specific training and is core to service robotics, warehouse logistics, and autonomous exploration. Existing approaches are observed to fail to achieve genuine zero-shot generalization: explicit-map methods rely on accurate reconstruction and are sensitive to sensor noise; supervised policies memorize training-scene patterns and degrade under illumination, furniture, and layout shifts; implicit representations offer continuous, differentiable encoding but remain confined to passive reconstruction and lack effective coupling with active decisions. To address this, EBM-Nav is proposed as a zero-shot navigation framework built on an energy-based model. Specifically, a periodic-activation implicit scene encoder is employed to map discrete RGB-D observations into a continuous, differentiable representation supporting arbitrary-resolution spatial queries. An energy function over the observation–action–goal triple is designed to reformulate navigation as gradient descent on an energy landscape. A frozen multimodal large language model is integrated to decompose long-horizon instructions into subgoals and generate candidate directions. A contrastive-divergence learning mechanism is developed with short-step Langevin dynamics to efficiently construct negative samples for training the energy function. Systematic experiments are conducted on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE continuous vision-and-language navigation benchmarks, and it is shown that EBM-Nav significantly outperforms state-of-the-art zero-shot methods in success rate, path efficiency, and navigation accuracy, while providing an interpretable energy-confidence mechanism for decisions. These results verify the energy-landscape zero-shot navigation paradigm, offer a general learning paradigm for embodied intelligence, and extend energy-based models from static perception to sequential decision-making, with methodological implications for service robots and autonomous exploration.

nodes.name: Feasibility of a Multimodal Lifestyle Intervention Programme for Patients With Ulcerative Colitis: A Single‐Arm Pilot Study
nodes.venue: JCC Plus
nodes.abstract: Plain Language Summary Lifestyle factors, such as exercise, diet and mental health, have shown promise in improving well‐being in people with ulcerative colitis, a chronic inflammatory condition of the large bowel. However, these factors are usually addressed separately in research. Therefore, we explored whether a 24‐week programme combining exercise, personalised dietary advice and psychological support could be implemented in people with ulcerative colitis. Thirty patients took part in the programme. Most participants remained in the study, and three‐quarters were satisfied with the programme. However, maintaining participation across the different components proved challenging. In particular, adherence to the exercise programme was low, whereas adherence to dietary advice was higher. More than half of the participants were eligible for psychological support, but only a quarter of those started the programme. No unexpected safety concerns were observed. Overall, our findings suggest that patients may be interested in a broad lifestyle approach, but that initial interest does not necessarily translate into sustained participation. Therefore, future programmes should focus on making lifestyle interventions more flexible, practical and tailored to individual people.

nodes.name: Pasture area increases livestock rabies risk in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: a geospatial analysis of neurological syndrome cases (2020–2024)
nodes.venue: Tropical Animal Health and Production
nodes.abstract: Abstract Animal rabies poses a risk to livestock in Brazil due to transmission by hematophagous bats. The Brazilian sanitary surveillance system mandates rabies testing for any livestock exhibiting signs of neurological syndrome. This geospatial, retrospective, longitudinal, observational study analyzed rabies test results for 204 cattle and 56 horses presenting with neurological syndrome in Rio de Janeiro State, Brazil, from 2020 to 2024. We calculated correlations and linear models between rabies results and municipal land-use types, as well the population of herbivores. Most neurological syndrome cases and positive rabies results occurred in cattle. The final linear model for the number of neurological syndrome cases and positive rabies results incorporated pasture area, shrub area and cattle population. Pasture area was positively correlated with higher numbers ( p = 0.011 and p = 0.005, respectively). Larger shrub area was associated with fewer neurological syndrome reports and fewer positive results ( p = 0.009 and p = 0.010, respectively). Greater cattle population showed a negative association with neurological syndrome notifications and positive detections ( p = 0.085 and p = 0.046, respectively).A higher proportion of positive rabies tests was associated with larger pasture areas ( p = 0.019) and with lower equine populations ( p = 0.115). These findings indicate that the lower animal diversity in pasture areas provides few alternative feeding options for Desmodus rotundus besides livestock, leading to more neurological syndrome cases and animal rabies infections. A larger shrub area offer feed alternatives other than cattle to the bats and a larger cattle population dilutes the frequency of bat meals across individuals, reducing both neurological syndrome notifications and positive rabies detections.

nodes.name: Dual-tapered graded-index two-mode fiber and peak-detection improvement algorithm for refractive index sensing
nodes.venue: Applied Optics
nodes.abstract: Dual tapers based on a graded-index (GI) two-mode (TM) fiber are proposed for refractive index (RI) sensing in this work. Sensitivity of 1433.94 nm/RIU with R 2 =0.98 is achieved using the direct peak-finding method, where the sensitivity enhancement originated from two guided modes and corresponding two sets of excited cladding modes. To improve wavelength demodulation accuracy, spatial frequency concentration algorithm is presented to filter out the influence of optical intensity fluctuations and mode noise via a bandpass filter, and yielding the sensing sensitivity 1669.61 nm/RIU and R 2 =0.9699 after data processing. Furthermore, empirical mode decomposition (EMD) is utilized to decompose transmission spectra according to their noise features. By calculating correlation coefficients between each intrinsic mode function and the raw spectrum, noise components are eliminated to smooth the spectra. The EMD-processed spectra produce the sensing sensitivity of 1458.52 nm/RIU with R 2 =0.9930 through peak-finding again. Experimental results demonstrate that the GI two-mode fiber enhances the sensing sensitivity of tapered fiber sensors, while the EMD algorithm improves the sensing accuracy. The results in this work could provide technical support for the practical sensing applications of tapered fiber sensors.

nodes.name: Roadmap for the Prosperity of the Parts Manufacturing Industry in Iran
nodes.venue: Future of Work and Digital Management Journal
nodes.abstract: The aim of this research was to develop a roadmap for the prosperity of the parts manufacturing industry in Iran. The present research is qualitative in terms of approach and developmental in terms of objective. The statistical population was in the form of an expert group, including officials and senior managers and experts familiar with the research topic, in the research area. In-depth interviews and group analysis were used to collect research data. The validity and reliability of the findings were examined and confirmed by external reviewers and triangulation. Reliability was also confirmed based on Cohen's Kappa index, with a numerical value of 0.726. In order to analyze the qualitative data, content analysis based on the data obtained from the interviews was used.The conceptual model consisted of 12 main aspects, including 146 indicators or concepts of the evaluator, which were obtained through the integration and classification of the tips or guide codes. The main dimensions in the model include: factors of production boom from the perspective of resources and infrastructure in the parts manufacturing industry within the model including 16 structures and 35 evaluators, factors of production boom from the perspective of technology in the parts manufacturing industry within the model including 8 structures (2 main and 6 secondary) and 19 evaluators, and factors of production boom from the perspective of trends and directions in product development in the parts manufacturing industry within the model including 12 structures and 34 evaluators. The final findings led to the creation of a strategic model in the form of a roadmap for production boom in longitudinal and functional directions that can be used as a comprehensive guide in line with the strategic direction in the said industry

Enhance EV station charge and discharge based on deep learning forecasting method incorporating renewable energy sources and multi-objective optimization algorithm
nodes.venue: International Journal of Renewable Energy Development
nodes.abstract: As electric vehicle charging station operations become more common, proper coordination of energy management is necessary to avoid high operational costs and carbon emissions caused by electric vehicle charging requirements, intermittent renewable sources, and fluctuating electricity rates. In this research, a forecast-based optimization methodology is created with the objective of optimizing the charge-discharge management of a renewable-powered electric vehicle charging station system involving photovoltaic generation, wind generation, fuel cells, electric vehicles, and stationary batteries. First, a recurrent neural network is used to predict relevant time series data, such as photovoltaic energy, wind energy, electric vehicle load demand, fuel cell energy production, and electric vehicle energy consumption. These forecasted data are then applied to a bi-objective energy management optimization problem, which is solved using NSGA-II. The objective is to minimize operating cost and emissions while considering power balance, grid energy exchange, and other operational constraints associated with the fuel cell, battery storage system, and electric vehicles. In this study, two scenarios are examined using one month of hourly data; Scenario 1 does not use stationary batteries, whereas Scenario 2 uses them. The forecasting results show robust predictions, with one-hour-ahead values ranging from 0.9162 to 0.9708. The optimization results show that Scenario 2 provides better energy shifting and peak-period support through battery charging and discharging management. Compared with Scenario 1, the operating cost is reduced from $171,833.86 to $160,388.44, and emissions are decreased from 13,485.48 kg to 12,892.23 kg, leading to 6.7% and 4.4% reductions, respectively.

A Semi‐Interpretable Multimodal Model Combining Electronic Health Records and Chest X‐Rays for <scp>COVID</scp> ‐19‐Related Death Prediction
nodes.venue: Expert Systems
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT Purpose Prognostic models can benefit from integrating heterogeneous data sources. While deep learning‐based multimodal models often improve predictive performance, their limited interpretability remains a barrier to clinical adoption. Moreover, achieving robust generalization with such models typically requires large and diverse datasets, which are not always available in clinical research. This study evaluated whether a late fusion model combining traditional statistical approaches with deep learning models could rival deep learning‐only multimodal models while preserving interpretability to support clinical use. Methods We conducted a retrospective single‐center cohort study of 965 hospitalized patients with laboratory‐confirmed SARS‐CoV‐2 infection who underwent frontal chest X‐ray imaging during hospitalization between March 2020 and January 2022. Of these, 64 (6.6%) died. Structured clinical data and chest X‐ray images were used to predict COVID‐19‐related death. We developed unimodal baseline models and two multimodal approaches: a deep learning‐based joint fusion model and a late fusion model leveraging logistic regression to combine predictions from the best‐performing models for every data modality. Given the limited sample size and class imbalance, performance was evaluated using repeated five‐fold cross validation. Results The late fusion model achieved the best overall performance, with the highest median test AUPRC of 0.363 (IQR 0.271–0.384) across cross validation folds, outperforming unimodal baselines based on structured clinical data or images alone. The late fusion model also outperformed the joint fusion model, achieving, respectively, a 3.1% and 3.6% relative improvement in AUPRC and Brier score on pooled out‐of‐sample predictions and yielding the highest balanced F1‐score. Moreover, it preserved partial interpretability by linking predictions to clinically meaningful variables such as age and comorbidities and enabling image‐based predictions to be traced back to radiographic abnormalities. Conclusions Late fusion models integrating statistical models for clinical data with deep learning for image classification can enhance prognostic performance over unimodal models without fully sacrificing interpretability. In settings with limited data, they may also outperform deep learning‐based joint fusion models. These findings support late fusion as a promising strategy that warrants prospective evaluation and external validation before clinical implementation.
